$comment: Configuration template for the qa pack. `agency add qa` copies it to <project>/.agency/qa.json and fills in what it can detect. This file is owned by the PROJECT — a pack upgrade never overwrites it.

repo.$comment_slug: owner/repo. Filled in from the git remote.

brief.$comment: WHAT TO TEST. This is the field that makes the specialist yours — the method is the same everywhere, the assignment is not.
brief.$comment_default: The standing brief: what holds for this project in every run. What the application is for, which flows are worth money, what has been fragile. `agency brief qa --set "…"` writes it here.
brief.$comment_scenarios: Named briefs for repeated sessions, e.g. {"smoke": "log in, open the dashboard, create one item"}. Run one with `agency run qa --scenario smoke`. Add one with `agency brief qa --scenario smoke --set "…"`. A one-off assignment does not belong here — that is `--prompt`.

app.$comment: Where the application under test lives. Without it the pack has nothing to open — `agency doctor` reports it as missing.
app.$comment_env: staging | local | production. Production is refused unless safety.allowProduction is true — a QA session writes data.
app.$comment_start: The command that starts the app locally, e.g. 'npm run dev'. Who may run it is decided by startPolicy.
app.$comment_startPolicy: manual = the agent must not start the app; if it is not running the run stops and says so. agent = it may start it itself and stop it afterwards.
app.$comment_readyCheck: A URL that returns 200 once the app is up, e.g. '/api/health'. Without it reachability is checked against baseUrl.
app.$comment_accountsFile: Test accounts and their roles. This file is NOT created by the installation and MUST NOT be committed — add `.agency/*.local.json` to .gitignore. Credentials never belong in the pack configuration.

playwright.$comment: How the session drives the browser. `agency add qa` fills this in from what the project already has — an existing Playwright setup is USED, not duplicated next to it. In VS Code: Specialists → QA → Browser.
playwright.$comment_enabled: false = the session only explores what it can reach over HTTP. true = it drives a real browser and writes reproduction specs.
playwright.$comment_configFile: The project's playwright.config.* if it has one. Its baseURL, projects, fixtures and auth setup are then reused — a spec that invents its own way of logging in is a second truth about the same thing.
playwright.$comment_projectTestDir: Where the project's own specs live. They are READ, for the dialect; the whole suite is not run — that is CI's job.
playwright.$comment_specTarget: run = reproduction specs are written into <RUN_DIR>/specs/ and travel with the run record, so a finding can be re-run a year later. suite = they are written into projectTestDir, i.e. into the project's own test suite. `run` changes nothing in the repository.
playwright.$comment_scaffold: What may happen when the project has no Playwright. never = stop and say so. run-dir = build a throwaway config inside the run directory (nothing is added to the repository). project = allowed to add playwright.config and the devDependency to the project.
playwright.$comment_command: How tests are started. Change it for a monorepo, e.g. "npm run -w web e2e".
playwright.$comment_headed: true = a visible browser. Useful when you want to watch the session, expensive when you do not.
playwright.$comment_artifacts: The trace is the strongest runtime evidence there is — it carries the DOM, the network and the console at the moment of failure. Artifacts land in <RUN_DIR>/evidence/ and are referenced from the finding.
playwright.$comment_storageStateFile: Signed-in browser state, so the session does not log in on every spec. It MUST NOT be committed — it is a session token. Add `.agency/*.local.json` to .gitignore.

$comment_personas: Who the agent pretends to be, e.g. [{"id": "new-user", "role": "visitor", "goal": "book the first lesson", "account": null}]. A finding found by two personas at once is worth more than a finding found twice by the same one.

session.$comment_budgetMinutes: How long one session may explore. When time runs out, what is already reproduced gets written — an unfinished session is a legitimate outcome, a lost one is not.
session.$comment_maxFindings: A ceiling, not a target. Zero findings is a valid result.
session.$comment_screenshots: Save screenshots into <RUN_DIR>/evidence/. They are the runtime evidence — without them a finding is a claim.

safety.$comment_allowDestructive: false = do not delete, do not cancel, do not pay for real. A QA session works with real data and there is no undo.
forbidden: emails, SMS or notifications to real users
changing or deleting data that does not belong to the test account

memory.$comment: The project's memory, not the pack's. Pages are OKF concepts in the knowledge bundle (`type: Page`, `status`, `stale_after`), so a conclusion that stopped holding can be marked instead of deleted. A project that already has this directory elsewhere keeps it — the path below is what the core reads. What has already been covered and what is known to be broken belongs to the project — that is exactly the split that let one QA agent grow into a specialist any project can hire.

agent.$comment: Who handles the session and with what. The model is a property of the task, not of the user. Override it for a single run with `agency run qa --model <m>`.

review.$comment: The shared output policy — every pack has this block: which dimensions run, what threshold a finding must clear, what language it is written in.
review.$comment_dimensions: access and regression are added once the project has test accounts with roles and a known-regressions file. Fewer dimensions is a legitimate outcome, not a failure.
review.$comment_minScore: Lower than the reviewer's 80 on purpose: a reproduced runtime failure is worth more than a static suspicion, and it was already filtered by having to be reproduced.
review.$comment_verifyCommand: What CI does. Used to drop findings CI would catch anyway — not to run anything.

sinks.$comment_runRecord: Always true. The run record is the truth, everything else is a derived sink — if a sink fails, the finding is not lost.
sinks.$comment_githubProject: The GitHub Project number for the one-way export, or null.
